Call prepare_owner_launch with actual parent context/start, exact selected owner contract/case/child role, fresh unique instance_id, and start_method=fork. Role is fork-guard and full role object must occur in contract; selected obligation/case checks remain as in Task2 capsule.

Prepare requires exact inherited environment including PYTEST_CURRENT_TEST call phase, active grant/source freeze, admitted Git executable, exact policy in prerequisite and CPU-bound justification/grant, actual fresh parent source witness and no held inherited metadata lock. Child receives actual opaque issued handle by fork.

Actual guard invokes record_fork_process(handle,start). Before reaching Git it verifies parent identity, one actual task, module hash, environment/argv/cwd, exact input/import bytes, active grant/freeze; writes exclusive owner claim and acquires its own metadata lock. Holding the lock elsewhere stalls before Git and is insufficient for this test.
proposed_hook: Save the real os.posix_spawn callable before replacement. Restrict the wrapper to the expected exact admitted Git executable and one of the two sealed query argvs; preserve all args, environment and file_actions. Other unexpected invocations are failures, not silently replaced executions.

Delegate once to the saved real callable. Use only the actual returned PID. Immediately send SIGSTOP to that actual PID using preloaded os.kill. Do not substitute a shell, wrapper executable, fake query, fabricated PID, stdout, or success status.

Observe /proc until bounded confirmation or failure: same live PID/start identity, stopped state from actual SIGSTOP, resolved /proc/PID/exe equal the admitted actual Git executable identity/bytes, exact cmdline query, actual PPID equal guard and expected owned PGID/session. Record actual UTC/monotonic observations and guard identity. A zombie/exited process, PID reuse, incorrect exe/group, or missed stop is a failed/UNRUN test setup, never proof of live Git.

Send a primitive pipe handshake with those actual observations; independently corroborate live/stopped Git membership from the supervisor before killing the guard. Prefer wait/poll/pipe primitives with finite test deadlines, preloaded before preparation. No Queue or imports.

Park the guard inside the wrapper after confirmed handshake and before returning Git PID to the recorder. Parent/supervisor issues SIGKILL to the exact owned guard identity only after live-Git confirmation. The stopped Git remains for actual P2 group cleanup.

Never send SIGCONT or perform supervisor cleanup to manufacture a passing cleanup result. If emergency cleanup is necessary after bounded P2 failure, record the case FAIL and clearly separate that cleanup from acceptance.

spawn_call_facts.actions: The original recorder builds two pipes and DUP2 actions to stdout/stderr, then CLOSE actions for enumerated open descriptors>2. A test hook must forward every argument and file action unchanged. A guard-owned test-handshake descriptor remains usable by the guard but the actual Git child is directed to close it.
spawn_call_facts.capture: The plan stores resolved admitted Git path, policy, refs, interpreter/imports and other parsed metadata. It does not store/capture a posix_spawn callable. os.posix_spawn attribute is read dynamically when each actual command is started.
spawn_call_facts.location: _sampler_command begins line587; actual os.posix_spawn call line598; record_fork_process begins646.
spawn_call_facts.module_checks: The guard checks module-name hash and actual inherited import paths/bytes. It does not capture os.posix_spawn in a closure or hash Python function attributes. This mechanical hookability is not a supported production mutation API or a semantic qualification exemption.
spawn_call_facts.timing: The recorder samples command start_ns, creates pipes/actions, then calls os.posix_spawn. Assignment to its local pid occurs only after the call returns. A wrapper that parks before returning leaves recorder pid=None; guard death prevents any finally cleanup. This deliberately exercises external P2 cleanup, not recorder-owned successful cleanup.

stall_limitations.bounds: The deliberately parked recorder cannot perform its own 3/6/8 deadline checks. This is a failure-path backstop test, never a successful guard sampler/whole-call proof. Root-approved test outer timeout and actual P2 bounded group cleanup must control the injected stop; success requires actual cleanup and lease ordering.
stall_limitations.no_production_stall: There is no frozen P3 API for deterministic pausing of a real Git process after exec. The proposed wrapper is explicit test-only fault injection.
stall_limitations.ownership: Guard /proc handshake is test observation, not a P0 completed process or signed authority. The independent supervisor must verify actual observed process identities, group and exit/reap/absence records.
stall_limitations.race: Even the first post-posix_spawn SIGSTOP can lose to a fast real Git exit. The hook guarantees truthful detection, not that every attempt captures a live process. A failed capture cannot be relabeled a valid backstop trial; retain it and obtain separate approval if stronger observation/exec-stop instrumentation is needed.

two_cases.assertions: Both cases must correlate actual controller/guard/Git PID-start-host-boot identities, query argv, group/session, stop handshake, guard death, P2 cleanup trigger, actual Git exit/group disappearance and lease-close ordering. Observe actual available wait/reap custody according to process ancestry; a nonparent supervisor cannot claim waitpid reap it did not perform.
two_cases.controller_exit: After verified live Git and actual guard SIGKILL, drive the existing actual controller-exit path. P2 must detect its real controller terminal status, kill the owned residual group including stopped Git, observe the required exit/group-empty/reap custody, then close/release its leases. Exact controller behavior and cleanup API are P2-owned test design.
two_cases.job_timeout: After verified live Git and actual guard SIGKILL, retain the controller in a bounded inert wait so actual sealed P2 job timeout fires. P2 must perform its timeout cleanup against the same observed owned group and remove stopped Git before lease close. Do not emulate timeout by manufacturing terminal records.
